findings.title: No double-checked cache lookup after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: The fast path reads entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, then releases it and takes the write Lock with no re-check. Any goroutine that missed the cache while another goroutine was already populating it will still re-read and re-parse assets-manifest.json from disk, one at a time, even though the cache is now filled. At startup, N concurrent requests produce N serialized manifest reads. Re-checking `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil` after taking the Lock would return the cached value immediately.

findings.title: Exclusive lock held across file I/O serializes all dev-mode calls and ignores caller context
findings.body: The write Lock is taken on every call in dev mode (cfg.Env == setting.Dev), because the early return is skipped. Each call then reads and parses the manifest from disk while holding the exclusive lock, so concurrent dev requests that previously ran in parallel now run one at a time. In non-dev mode, while the cache is nil (for example, the manifest is missing or failed to load), every request blocks on Lock without honouring its ctx, so a slow operation inside readWebAssetsFromCDN (which uses http.DefaultClient with no timeout) holds up all waiters. The CDN path is currently unreachable because cdn is the constant "", so this is latent, but the lock scope is wider than the data race requires. Doing the I/O outside the lock and only taking the lock to publish the result would avoid both problems.

findings.title: No regression test for concurrent access to the cached web assets
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on the package-level entryPointAssetsCache, but adds no test that exercises GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines. Without a test run under `go test -race`, nothing guards against the race being reintroduced, for example by a future change that reads the global outside the lock. A small test that calls GetWebAssets concurrently with a temp manifest, with the cache reset between cases, would lock in the fix.
